text: PHILIP MORRIS U.S.A.
INTER-OFFICE CORRESPONDENCE
QUALITY ENGINEERING
RICHMOND, VIRGINIA
TO:
J. L. Calloway
DATE: Oct. 15, 1992
FROM:
G. HoIguin
SUBJECT:
EVALUATE QUALITY IMPACT AND APPROPRIATE REJECT LIMITS FOR LIGHT WEIGHT
CIGARETTES
Introduction:
In an effort to respond to questions regarding the appropriate
light weight reject limit and the maximum rod weight reduction
achievable while maintaining the integrity and quality of our
product, the following test plan is submitted for review.
Objective:
To determine the appropriate cigarette rod Tight weight
reject limit. i.e. at what lighter than target cigarette rod
weight is the quality impacted to the point where the
product becomes unacceptable and should be rejected.
To determine the maximum amount of filler weight that can be
removed from the target weight cigarettes such as with the
ATM enabled before quality or machinability "problems" start
to occur and make the cigarette undesirable for our
customers.
To determine if there is any significant difference in the
quality of the cigarettes that are rejected at the light
weight reject Timit (-67 mg) when compared to cigarettes
that are made at a target weight that corresponds to the
light weight reject limit (target weight - 67 mg).
Test Procedure:
There are several conditions that must be met prior to
starting the evaluation and are listed below:
a)
The Marlboro blend (1l-2-92) will be initially used for
the evaluation.
b)
The test maker must have an Accuray weight controller.
c)
The test maker will produce, at different periods,
cigarettes other than Marlboro. i.e. two different
blends should be processed on the test maker, Marlboro
and a second blend.
An R&D model will be used to obtain background information
for predicting the quality impact on the cigarette rod
as blend components are changed and/or filler is removed.
The Marlboro filler blend model will be changed to
incorporate various filler weight reductions to the rod
target to determine the impact on the quality parameters.
(This step is expected to take 1-2 hours to complete.)
After obtaining the theoretical impact on the cigarette
quality as the filler is removed, testing will be performed
in a production environment.
